newsitem.title: USA: Three big brokers report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Three big brokers report higher earnings.

text.p: Three big brokerage houses reported higher third-quarter earnings Tuesday, though business was not as robust as in the previous quarter because of summer weakness in the stock and bond markets.

Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc., the nation's largest brokerage, said earnings rose 10 percent in the quarter, Donaldson Lufkin Jenrette Inc. reported a 34 percent gain and Painewebber Group Inc. said its earnings edged higher.

The brokerages had a strong first half as the stock market soared to new highs early in the year. While third-quarter results were above year-ago levels, they came in lower than the second quarter at all three firms.
Merrill said net earnings rose to $331 million, or $1.69 a share, from $300 million, or $1.47 a share, in the 1995 period. Merrill had earned $433 million, or $2.19 a share, in the second quarter.
Net revenues grew 15 percent to $3.09 billion and were the third-highest in Merrill's history, surpassed only by the first two quarters of 1996, the New York-based company said.
The third-quarter results were slightly better than expected on Wall Street but Merrill's stock edged lower anyway, down 25 cents to $68.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Investment banking revenues jumped 33 percent in the quarter on strong stock and bond underwriting, Merrill said, but commission revenues grew only 4 percent.
Painewebber said net income rose to $80.2 million from $78.2 million in the 1995 quarter. Earnings per share rose 79 cents from 71 cents. Painewebber had earned $92.2 million in the second quarter.
Net revenues fell 3.2 percent to $883.0 million from $912 million, reflecting the more difficult market environment, the New York-based company said.

"We are pleased with our third-quarter earnings, which surpassed the consensus estimates and represent consistent improvement despite uncertain markets in the quarter," Painewebber Chairman Donald Marron said in a statement.
Analysts had forecast that earnings per share would fall, according to First Call, which tracks estimates. Painewebber stock added 25 cents to $24.375 at midday on the NYSE.

New York-based DLJ said net income rose to $56.1 million, or 86 cents a share, from $42 million, or 72 cents a share, in the 1995 period. Net revenues grew 11 percent to $592 million. In the second quarter DLJ earned $97 million.
Analysts had forecast 82 cents a share, according to First Call, and DLJ stock added 87.5 cents to $33.75 on the Big Board.
DLJ, which is 80 percent owned by insurer The Equitable Cos. Inc., said underwriting revenues fell 11 percent to $130 million because of a slightly weaker market for new issues in the latest quarter.
All three brokerages said results for the first nine months set company records.
Merrill said its net earnings rose 45 percent to $1.17 billion from $810 million. Net revenues rose 27 percent to $9.74 billion from $7.65 billion.
Painewebber said earnings rose to $272.9 million in the period from $147.9 million in the 1995 period, excluding a one-time charge. Net revenues grew 13 percent to $2.80 billion from $2.46 billion.

DLJ said earnings in the first nine months rose 80 percent to $218.2 million, and stood 17 percent above its record full-year earnings of $186 million for 1993. Net revenues climbed 34 percent to $2 billion.
